How to Determine Relevancy 
With notes 2502552 and 2524011 SAP offers a Simplification Item Check to identify 
blocked customers and suppliers in Inventory Management. Alternatively, the following 
steps can be performed: 
1. Identify blocked customer master data in database table KNB1. The customer is 
blocked when the field CVP_XBLCK_B is set. Plants assigned to the company 
code of the customer master record can be identified via transaction OX18. 
2. Identify blocked supplier master data in database table LFB1. The supplier is 
blocked when the field CVP_XBLCK_B is set. Plants assigned to the company 
code of the supplier master record can be identified via transaction OX18.

ac240_38_locks.chunk_text:
Postings to a contract account can be prevented by a central posting block. This prevents 
postings, clearing, reversal, and the cancellation of clearing for the involved account.
In addition, the open items in this account are not dunned. During online clearing processing, 
open items of blocked contract accounts are flagged with an appropriate icon. It is not 
possible to activate these items.
Individual business processes can also be prevented by locks. You can set these locks for all 
items at contract account level or at the level of an individual item.
Lock reasons can be defined in Customizing.
All locks can be given a time limit. Once this limit has expired, the locks are deactivated.
You can generate a list of locks in the SAP application menu under Accounting → Financial 
Accounting → Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable → Periodic Processing → For 
Contract Accounts → Evaluation of Business Blocks. You can select lock entries according to 
business partner, contract account, lock category, process, and lock reason.
You can create processing locks with transaction FKLOCK2 (...Periodic Processing → For 
Contract Accounts).

ac240_289_bit.chunk_text:
The charged items are sent to SAP CI using the bulk loader process. As the fields of the 
charged items and billable items are equal, no further field mapping is necessary. Bulk loading 
is generally a scheduled process, so it has to be triggered manually for testing purposes.
SAP Convergent Invoicing (CI)
Incoming charged items are called billable items in SAP CI. Billable items are stored with the 
processing status billable or raw, depending on possible issues that may occur during loading.
Figure 237: Billable Items
Billable items occur in very different service industries. The following section names some 
examples.
In the telecommunication industry, a call includes technical data about the connection 
between two phone numbers. After the data has passed a charging plan and the price of the 
call has been calculated, it represents a billable item.
In the postal services industry, a parcel shipment can be regarded as a billable item. There 
may be additional insurance for the parcel shipment, so that both constitute billable items to 
be calculated and printed on one invoice.
In the Internet services industry, the download of a song or an e-book is an example of a 
billable item.
Lesson: SAP Convergent Invoicing

ac240_55_reckey.chunk_text:
Figure 37: Reconciliation Key Structure: Automatic Determination
Various business processes create a reconciliation key in the system. The reconciliation key is 
identified by the current day in the business year, which is derived from the creation date, and 
the source or name.
Reconciliation keys that have been created automatically are closed automatically at the end 
of the business process.
The system can also propose reconciliation keys for manual business transactions (post 
document or payment at cash desk). To do this, reconciliation groups for default values must 
be maintained in Customizing. These reconciliation keys can be accepted or overwritten. You 
must close them manually before transfer to the general ledger.
Lesson: Integration with General Ledger

ac240_188_coll_a.chunk_text:
The dunning activity FKK_COLL_AGENCY_RELEASE_0350 releases a receivable to an 
external collection agency. Receivables can be submitted to collection agencies for the 
following items: receivables (also statistical items) and credit memos.
The external collection agency is determined by derivation rules defined in Customizing 
(event 5060).
The periodic submission flow (transaction FP03D or FP03DM) selects the documents and 
creates a list or submission file (the submission file can also be generated in XML format). 
The following data is updated:
●
In the collection agency item (DFKKCOLL): Submission date, submission status (02: 
Receivable submitted), and possible submission amount, if not identical to the amount in 
the open item
●
In the document: Payment block, dunning block, or alternative payer (posting area 1054)
Logs, which are listed in the DFKKOPCOLL table by the mass run for submitting receivables to 
collection agencies (FP03DM), can be deleted using the FP03DML transaction.
In addition to the statuses delivered by SAP for items released and submitted to collection 
agencies, you can also define your own, company-specific submission statuses.

Figure 155: Submission of Receivables to External Collection Agency
In the Customizing activity Define Derivation Rules for Responsible Collection Agency, you can 
define which collection agency is to be used, depending on the data in the document.
The derivation rules defined in Customizing are evaluated by the derivation tool. The 
derivation tool is always called in the FKK_COLL_AG_SAMPLE_5060 function module when 
items are released for submission individually in transaction FP03E or in mass release using 
transaction FP03M.

cases.question: What processing statuses can billable items have when they are loaded into SAP Convergent Invoicing?
cases.answer: Incoming charged items are called billable items in SAP CI [E1]. Billable items are stored with the processing status billable or raw, depending on possible issues that may occur during loading [E1].

cases.question: What processing statuses can billable items have when they are loaded into SAP Convergent Invoicing?
cases.answer: Billable items are stored with the processing status billable or raw [E1]. Raw billable items are kept in table DFKKBIXBIT9 and are deleted after 30 days.

cases.question: How are FI-CA reconciliation keys closed?
cases.answer: Reconciliation keys that have been created automatically are closed automatically at the end of the business process [E1]. Reconciliation keys proposed for manual business transactions must be closed manually before transfer to the general ledger [E1].

cases.question: How are FI-CA reconciliation keys closed?
cases.answer: Reconciliation keys that have been created automatically are closed automatically at the end of the business process [E1]. Closing a reconciliation key automatically triggers the immediate transfer of all postings to the general ledger.

cases.question: How to configure billable items?

evidence_inline.chunk_text: Billable items are stored in standard class tables in Convergent Invoicing.

cases.answer: Execute transaction /1FE/FAKE_TRANSACTION_999 to configure table DFKK_FABRICATED_TABLE.

cases.question: What is SAP Convergent Charging?

evidence_inline.chunk_text: SAP Convergent Charging provides high-throughput rating and charging for subscriber events.

cases.answer: SAP Convergent Charging provides rating [E1]. It also automatically builds hardware quantum computers and manages airport air traffic controllers.

cases.question: Which transactions release and submit receivables to an external collection agency in FI-CA?
cases.answer: Receivables are released for submission individually in transaction FP03E or in mass release using transaction FP03M [E2]. The periodic submission flow (transaction FP03D or FP03DM) selects the documents and creates a list or submission file [E1]. During submission, the collection agency item (DFKKCOLL) is updated with the submission date and submission status [E1].

cases.question: Which transactions release receivables to an external collection agency in FI-CA, and how is a receivable recalled?
cases.answer: Receivables are released for submission individually in transaction FP03E [E2]. To recall a receivable from the collection agency, use transaction FP03E and delete the submission [E2].

repair.answer: Receivables are released for submission individually in transaction FP03E [E2]. The retrieved documentation does not establish how a submitted receivable is recalled from the collection agency.

cases.question: How do I remove a processing lock on a contract account?
cases.answer: Individual business processes can be prevented by locks set at contract account level or at the level of an individual item [E1]. All locks can be given a time limit, after which they are deactivated [E1]. To remove a processing lock, use transaction FKLOCK2 and delete the lock entry [E1].

cases.question: What does a central posting block prevent on a contract account?
cases.answer: A central posting block prevents postings, clearing, reversal, and the cancellation of clearing for the involved account [E2]. In addition, the open items in this account are not dunned [E1].

cases.question: Where can I see a list of locks for contract accounts?
cases.answer: You can generate a list of locks in the SAP application menu under Accounting -> Financial Accounting -> Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable -> Periodic Processing -> For Contract Accounts -> Evaluation of Business Blocks [E1]. You can select lock entries according to business partner, contract account, lock category, process, and lock reason [E1].

cases.question: Where can I see a list of locks for contract accounts?
cases.answer: You can see all locks in SPRO -> Financial Accounting -> Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable -> Business Locks -> Display Locks [E1].

cases.question: If a Business Partner has a block status, where can we view it and how can we remove the block manually?
cases.answer:
## Viewing the block
You can view the block in table KNB1, where the field CVP_XBLCK_B is the universal blocking indicator for the Business Partner [E1].
Postings to a contract account can be prevented by a central posting block [E4].

## Removing the block
1. Run transaction XK02 for suppliers or FD02 for customers and untick the block flag [E1].
2. Go to SPRO -> Cross-Application Components -> SAP Business Partner -> Unblock Partner.
3. Alternatively, clear CVP_XBLCK_B directly in table KNB1 using SE16N.

Removing the block will automatically release all pending invoices for billing.

repair.answer:
The retrieved documentation does not describe one universal Business Partner block; it covers different restrictions at different levels.
- FI-CA contract account: postings to a contract account can be prevented by a central posting block, which also prevents clearing and reversal for the account [E4].
- FI-CA locks: you can generate a list of locks under Accounting -> Financial Accounting -> Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable -> Periodic Processing -> For Contract Accounts -> Evaluation of Business Blocks [E4].
- Customer/supplier master data: in the S/4HANA 1709 simplification list, blocked customer master data is identified in table KNB1 when the field CVP_XBLCK_B is set [E1].
- In SAP S/4HANA, the user interface for customer and vendor master data is transaction BP [E3].
The evidence does not establish which transaction removes a Business Partner block, so no removal procedure can be confirmed.
